**Treasury Yield Curve Edges Wider as 30-Year Reaches 5.10%**

The 2s10s spread moved to 36 basis points on 2026-07-13, a modest shift that keeps long-duration financing costs in focus.

**Why it matters:** Longer maturities combine expectations for future short rates with duration supply, inflation uncertainty and term-premium compensation.

Full analysis: https://capitalchronicle.substack.com/p/treasury-yield-curve-edges-wider

For informational purposes only; not financial advice.

linkedin.text:
Treasury Yield Curve Edges Wider as 30-Year Reaches 5.10%

The 2s10s spread moved to 36 basis points on 2026-07-13, a modest shift that keeps long-duration financing costs in focus.

The mechanism: Longer maturities combine expectations for future short rates with duration supply, inflation uncertainty and term-premium compensation.

The policy context: The 2-year sector is more exposed to the expected policy path, while the 30-year sector carries much more duration and fiscal-supply risk.

Read the full Capital Chronicle analysis: https://capitalchronicle.substack.com/p/treasury-yield-curve-edges-wider

x.full_text:
Treasury Yield Curve Edges Wider as 30-Year Reaches 5.10%

The 30-year Treasury par yield reached 5.10% as the 2s10s slope edged to 36 basis points.

https://capitalchronicle.substack.com/p/treasury-yield-curve-edges-wider

Why it matters: The long end reflects future-rate expectations, duration supply and term-premium compensation; a one-basis-point slope change is context, not a regime call.

For informational purposes only; not financial advice.

Policy context: The 2-year and 30-year maturities carry different policy and duration sensitivities. Cross-asset context: Long rates can influence discount rates and financing benchmarks.
